_what: FEATURE SPEC: EYES (felid pack, case cat1, Phase 2 Stage 3). Globe, lids wrapping the globe, third eyelid, periocular coat; an SDF construction recipe in the head frame and a geometric probe per inventory part. Written by the 'eyes' builder (spec only, no geometry).
status: spec (self-checked against the photo and Phase 1; not independently reviewed)
criteria: C5 positions/sizes (photo where it sees, else Phase 1 within uncertainty, else anatomy)
C6 eyes are globes with lids on them
C3/C3b the eye is furless and sits ON the envelope; no goggle eyes
C4 inventory part 'eyelids wrapping the globe, third eyelid at the inner corner' visible in clay
frame: partition.head_local(world) * 1000 = head-frame mm: x = the cat's LEFT, y = BACK (the face points -y), z = UP. Tripo world: z-up metres, faces -y.
evidence_ranking: photo where it sees > constraints (lid margin ON the globe) > Tripo/Phase 1 numbers with their uncertainty > cited anatomy > estimate (flagged). One argued exception: the CORNEA CURVATURE is cited anatomy over Tripo's cap quadric, because Phase 1 shows Tripo has no globe (a painted shell) and its flat cap (sphere-equivalent r ~14.7 mm) cannot carry a 16.5 mm cornea; G3 'never copy Tripo artefacts as anatomy'. The photo's crisp corneal highlight supports a strongly curved cornea.

inputs.photo: cases/cat1/ref.jpg (each eye ~40-47 px across; 0.367-0.381 mm/px at the eyes)

registration_tripo_to_camera_world_m.note: translation only (camera rotation used as frozen). Residual < 1 px on the fitted points; the nose leather lands 4 px from the builder's nose point. The two differ by 4 % in scale (0.381 vs 0.367 mm/px) - reported as the photo-scale uncertainty. Tripo's painted irises sit off-centre in their margins (L 1.8 mm medial, R 3.3 mm lateral), so iris-centre registration shifts the margins ~2.5 mm in x; the fissure-midpoint registration is preferred for outlines. Camera view direction in the head frame: (0.023, 0.961, -0.276) - the photo sees the face from 16 deg above the head-frame horizontal, ~14 deg off each eye's axis.

inputs.phase1: tripo_rebuild/layers/eyes.json (margin_head_mm, canthi, fissure), tripo_rebuild/REVIEW_eyes.md (B1 lid height, B2 overhang, S1 crease angle, S2 slant, S4 wall top)

photo_findings.opening_shape: near-round, wide-open eyes: inner dark-rim ellipse R 35.0 x 40.2 px, L 35.8 x 42.3 px (rms 0.4-0.5 px) = ~13 x 15.5 mm; Tripo's margin is a squinted almond (11.6-11.7 mm tall). The photo wins on the opening height (lower lid ~0.8 mm lower); Tripo keeps the canthi (an ellipse fit cannot resolve the pointed corners, and the medial wedge is excluded by the tracer).
photo_findings.dark_margin_band: a continuous dark (pigmented) rim round the whole opening, 2.3-3.5 px = 0.85-1.3 mm wide face-on (median radial 2.25 px on L; R inflated by a tear stain), then a 0.4-0.8 mm pinkish sparse-haired band, then white fur. Read: hairless pigmented lid margin plus the lid wall seen at a grazing angle.
photo_findings.third_eyelid: L medial canthus: a pale wedge 1-2 px wide (0.4-0.7 mm) over ~6 rows (2 mm) between the dark rim and the iris (Lab L 138-165 between rims of L < 80; rows y 318-324). R medial canthus: none visible (dark, tear-stain pigment running down). Matches 'third eyelid pale pink at the inner corner, hidden when alert' (cat-anatomy.md).
photo_findings.cornea: a crisp specular highlight on both eyes, upper-lateral of the pupil (R ~(659,301) px, L ~(767,302) px) = a smooth, strongly curved glossy cornea.
photo_findings.pupil: vertical slit-ellipse 12 x 19 px (4.5 x 7 mm), ~1.2-1.7 mm medial and ~1.3 mm above the globe apex (registration-dependent): pigment/iris texture for Stage 4, not geometry. If an iris solid is wanted, its plane sits ~4.5-5 mm behind the corneal apex (ESTIMATE from the corneal sag 5.7 mm; flagged).

globe_derivation: cornea sphere r = 8.82 mm; limbus radius a = 8.25 mm (corneal diameter 16.5 x 16.2, Carrington 1986 via cat-anatomy.md) -> corneal sag = r - sqrt(r^2 - a^2) = 5.70 mm. Axial length L = 19.75 mm = RS + sqrt(RS^2 - a^2) + 5.70 -> RS = 9.45 mm; limbus plane 4.61 mm in front of the sclera centre, cornea centre 1.48 mm in front of it, apex 10.30 mm in front. Equatorial globe diameter 18.9 mm (derived; cat-anatomy.md's 'globe ~21 mm' is the upper end; acceptable range 18.9-21 - a 21 mm globe with the same cornea only moves the posterior pole ~1 mm deeper).

lids.model: each lid is a SKIN FOLD resting on the globe: inner face = palpebral conjunctiva lying ON the globe (contact gap 0.05 mm so the globe can rotate and the lids can blink), free margin hairless and pigmented, outer face = face skin running into the periocular skin. Upper and lower lid are one ring joined at the canthi.

margin_thickness_mm.source: PHOTO: the dark pigmented band is 0.85-1.3 mm wide face-on (the margin's intermarginal face plus the wall seen nearly edge-on). No cited cat value found (searched: cat eyelid thickness histology; only human/ox values).

canthi.lateral: a V (Phase 1 eyes.py docstring: 'the outer corner is a V'); the 0.45 mm edge radius still applies

lids.no_eyelashes: cats have no cilia; 'the first row of skin hairs are adapted for the same purpose' (Dechra, via cat-hair-streams.md) - a Stage 5 hair item, not geometry

third_eyelid.what: nictitating membrane: a conjunctival fold on a T-shaped cartilage whose crossbar stiffens the free edge and curves to hug the cornea; it lies in the ventromedial fornix and can cover the whole cornea (PMC10508502; fupress IJAE 1319)
third_eyelid.presence: BOTH eyes as structure (anatomy); exposed at the medial canthus only, as a sliver: photo L 0.4-0.7 mm, photo R not visible (0-0.5 mm; hidden or pigmented) -> build an exposed width of 0.5 mm on both eyes (L from the photo; R by symmetry, flagged)
third_eyelid.shape: a thin curved crescent shell lying on the globe (gap 0.05 mm), leading edge concave toward the cornea (arc radius 6 mm, estimate), running from the medial canthus ~3 mm along the lower margin and ~1.5 mm along the upper margin before disappearing under the lids; the hidden body continues 4 mm under the medial lid into the fornix

thickness_mm.source: ESTIMATE (no feline value found; searched cat third eyelid size / cartilage)

third_eyelid.colour_note: pale pink (cat-anatomy.md; photo L pale wedge) - Stage 4 pigment, not geometry

lid_margin_band.source: PHOTO: dark hairless band 0.85-1.3 mm; coat.json furless eye_opening ramp 1.5 mm

lid_skin_and_periocular.zone: within 3 mm of the margin, back to the region depth over 10 mm more (coat_field.py PERI_IN 3 mm, PERI_W 10 mm)
lid_skin_and_periocular.source: coat_field.py PERIOCULAR_MM = 0.75 (ESTIMATE from the orchestrator brief 'about 0.5-1 mm'); PHOTO: a 0.4-0.8 mm sparse-haired pinkish band, then very short white fur - consistent, but not measurable as a fringe at 0.37 mm/px

periocular_coat.interface_note: coat_field.py's eye_opening mask still uses the Phase 1 margin polygon. With this spec the lower lid margin sits ~0.8 mm lower, so the furless mask must use lid_margin.outline_head_mm, or the lower lid gets fur on its pigmented margin. Not edited here (the skin agent owns coat_field and the skin).

sdf_recipe.units: head-frame mm; sdf < 0 inside. smin(a,b,k) = polynomial smooth min; smax(a,b,k) = -smin(-a,-b,k). Per eye, with the eye frame (n, u, v), sclera centre Cs and cornea centre Cc from eyes[...].globe.
steps: 1 GLOBE (its own closed object, NOT unioned with the skin): G(p) = smin(|p-Cs| - 9.45, |p-Cc| - 8.82, k=0.8). The k=0.8 blend makes the limbal sulcus; the corneal radius stays 8.82 within 4 mm of the apex.

2 EYE COORDS: q = p - Cs; U = 9.45*atan2(q.u, q.n), V = 9.45*atan2(q.v, q.n). M(p) = signed 2-D distance from (U,V) to the polygon lid_margin.outline_UV_mm (+ outside the opening, on the lid side). h(p) = G(p) (height above the globe).
3 OVERHANG o(phi): phi = polar angle of (U,V) about the opening centre; o = 0.4 mm, raised smoothly to 1.0 mm within 25 deg of the medial canthus and to 0.6 mm within 25 deg of the lateral canthus.
4 LID SHELL: Sh(p) = max(h - H, 0.05 - h) with H = 1.9 mm (skin value, lids.height_above_eye_surface); keep it to the lid zone: Sh = smax(Sh, M - 6.0, k=1.5) (fades into the face beyond ~6 mm).

5 OPENING CUT with lean: Lid(p) = max(Sh, -(M + o*clamp(h/1.2, 0, 1) + 0.45)); ROUND: Lid_r = Lid - 0.45 (0.45 mm radius on the free edge; the +0.45 in the cut keeps the crease on the margin polygon). The inner face leans over the globe by o for h >= 1.2 mm.

6 SKIN EDIT (applied to the Stage 2 skin S; S itself is read-only here): S1 = max(S, -Tunnel) with Tunnel(p) = max(M, -h - 0.5, h - 6.0) (removes the cap/envelope skin covering the opening, from 0.5 mm behind the globe surface to 6 mm in front); S2 = smax(S1, 0.05 - G(p), k=0.3) (the socket: the skin never comes closer than 0.05 mm to the globe).

7 LIDS INTO THE SKIN: S3 = smin(S2, Lid_r, k=1.0): the outer lid face runs into the periocular skin; k = 1.0 is the soft slope from the wall top into the face (Tripo's profile turns > 60 deg at the wall top, REVIEW_eyes B1).

8 THIRD EYELID (own object, or smin into S3 with k=0.2): TEL(p) = max(|h - 0.35| - 0.3, Cr(U,V), M - 4.0, -M - 6.0), where Cr(U,V) = 6.0 - |(U,V) - (Pmed + (0.5 + 6.0)*e_med)| clips a crescent (Pmed = the medial canthus in (U,V), e_med = unit vector from Pmed toward the opening centre); round its leading edge by 0.3 mm with the same offset trick as step 5. Exposed width at the canthus = 0.5 mm.
9 FORNIX: the lid's inner face (the h = 0.05 shell surface) continues under the skin to M = +4.0 (step 4's shell already covers it); nothing more to add for clay.
do_not: copy Tripo's cap quadric as the cornea (shell artefact)
use eyes.json lid_step 0.5 mm or crease 75-78 deg (REVIEW_eyes B1/S1)
paint a dark ring in place of the lid margin (E5)
union the globe into the skin (the globe must rotate; 'lids cut through the globe' is C6's planted failure)

probes._how: measured on the BUILT mesh (skin + lids + globe + third eyelid), head frame, exact plane sections (tripo_rebuild exact-section tools), never on vertex rings; each with expected value and tolerance. Phase 1 eyes.py must be re-pointed at our mesh (A16) and fixed per REVIEW_eyes B1/B2 before its numbers count.

globe.probe: corneal radius: circle fit to the globe's section through the axis n, central +-4 mm, two perpendicular planes
apex position (furthest globe point along n)
axial length: apex to posterior pole along n
limbus: the crease ring between the cornea and sclera spheres, its diameter
the globe is a separate closed manifold and does not come through the skin outside the opening: count skin vertices with M > 0.5 and G < 0
corneal highlight: render with the photo light (cases/cat1/light.json) through the frozen camera
globe.expected: a specular spot upper-lateral of the pupil on both eyes
globe.tol: within 5 px of the photo's (R ~(659,301), L ~(767,302) px)

lid_margin.probe: crease = where the built surface leaves the globe (d > 0.1 mm) on sections perpendicular to the margin (plane spanned by the globe normal and the outward tangent), 48 stations
fissure height in the eye frame (V extent of the crease)
photo outline: render through the frozen camera (fissure-midpoint registration), trace the inner dark-rim / globe boundary with radial profiles, fit an ellipse

lids.probe: lid height: wall-top turn point (direction > 60 deg toward outward; also report 45 deg) on the 48 perpendicular sections, height above the globe
lids.envelope_check: after fur (Stage 5) the fur surface there stands 2.0-2.4 mm above Tripo's cap (REVIEW_eyes B1)

lids.probe: overhang: occlusion of globe points by non-globe faces along the globe normal (REVIEW_eyes B2 method), hidden width per station
lids.planted: a vertical lid (o = 0) must read 0 hidden width; a 20 deg lean must read > 0.3 mm

lids.probe: crease interior angle (0-0.8 mm chord) between the globe tangent and the lid's inner face
no gap and no penetration between the lid's inner face and the globe: distance from lid inner-face vertices (M in [0, 4]) to the globe
margin thickness: lid width on each section at h = 1.0 mm
clay render (E5, A17): front, three-quarter and side close-ups, X-ray off: the lid reads as a raised rounded rim casting a contact shadow on the globe all round; no painted ring

third_eyelid.probe: exists as structure: a section through the medial canthus perpendicular to the margin shows a membrane edge between the globe and the medial lid
exposed width along the fissure axis at the medial canthus, seen along n
photo-camera render: pale wedge at the L medial canthus (Lab L > 135 between the dark rim and the iris)
third_eyelid.tol: present on L; may be absent on R

periocular_coat.probe: coat depth on the lid margin band (0-1 mm outside the crease)
coat depth 1.5-3 mm outside the crease
C3b goggle-eye check: skin-to-envelope distance in the ring 3-13 mm outside the crease rises monotonically from 0.75 to the region depth, no step > 0.3 mm

open_and_conflicts: PHOTO vs TRIPO on the opening height: the photo's opening is ~1.0-1.5 mm taller (lower lid lower). Taken from the photo (J2) via k_low 1.18 +- 0.06; the upper lid is kept from Tripo (agrees within 0.6 mm).

Photo scale depends on the Tripo-to-camera registration (translation only): 0.367-0.381 mm/px (4 %). A rotation+scale registration on more landmarks (ears, chin) would tighten it; not done (time cap).

Cornea curvature from anatomy overrides Tripo's flat cap (argued in evidence_ranking). Consequence: the cornea stands ~1.1 mm in front of Tripo's cap at the centre - the furless eye on the envelope (C3) must be checked against OUR globe, not the Tripo cap, and the skin agent's surface over the opening is removed by recipe step 6.
Globe axis taken from the Tripo margin plane (symmetric L/R). Cat optic-axis divergence was not researched (Bishop, Kozak & Vakkur 1962 has it; full text not read).
Lid margin thickness, fornix depth, third-eyelid thickness and crescent radius: no cited feline values found - estimates, flagged low.
Periocular coat depth 0.75 mm: estimate (no cited source); the photo is consistent but not a measurement.
coat_field.py's eye_opening mask uses the old (Phase 1) margin; it needs lid_margin.outline_head_mm (interface note).

sources.axial_length: https://busqueda.bvsalud.org/portal/resource/es/mdl-22280390 (PMID 22280390, Konrade et al. 2012) - A-mode ultrasound, 98 normal domestic cats: axial globe length 19.75 +- 1.59 mm
sources.cornea_diameter_globe_orbit: engine/references/cat-anatomy.md (Carrington 1986: cornea 16.5 x 16.2 mm; globe ~21 mm; orbit 24-28 mm; fissure 20-28 mm; third eyelid pale pink at the inner corner, hidden when alert; upper lid half almond, lower lid round, outer corners slightly higher - CFA)

sources.lids_hair: engine/references/cat-hair-streams.md - no cilia; 'the first row of skin hairs are adapted' (Dechra Anatomy of the Eye: Upper and Lower Lids); lids haired outside, conjunctiva inside (Reighard & Jennings 1901)
